name: Mommy Makeover
imageAlt: Woman in a champagne satin wrap dress with her hands clasped at the waist, illustrating the mommy makeover with Dr. Fulvio Correa in Cartagena
description: Mommy makeover in Cartagena: tummy tuck, breast surgery and liposuction in one plan. Who is a candidate, recovery by week, and how long to stay.
summary:
A **mommy makeover in Colombia** is a personalized combination of body procedures—most often a tummy tuck, breast surgery (lift, implants, reduction or a mix) and liposuction—planned to address the changes that pregnancy, childbirth and breastfeeding leave behind. The American Society of Plastic Surgeons (ASPS) notes that it is typically performed as a single-stage operation, with the number of procedures limited to what is safe for each patient.

It is not a fixed package. Two women can both be told they need a "mommy makeover" and end up with very different plans: one may need abdominal muscle repair and a breast lift, another only liposuction and implants. The plan follows your anatomy, your health history and the help you can count on at home.

Dr. Fulvio Correa evaluates every mommy makeover patient, whether she lives in Colombia or travels from the United States; the first consultation can be in person in Cartagena or virtual, before any trip is arranged. The sections below cover who tends to be a good candidate, what the surgery can combine, what recovery usually looks like in published medical guidance, and how to plan a trip that leaves enough room for healing. When you are ready, you can [request a consultation](/en/book-consultation/?procedure=mommy-makeover) to review your own case.
candidates:
ASPS lists four starting points for mommy makeover candidacy: you are in good medical health, you are at or near your ideal body weight, you have realistic expectations, and **you are finished having children**. The last one matters because a future pregnancy can stretch the abdomen and change the breasts again.

Other signals that usually make planning more predictable:

- **A stable weight.** Mayo Clinic advises keeping a stable weight for roughly 6 to 12 months before a tummy tuck, since large changes afterward alter the result.
- **Time after breastfeeding.** For breast lifts, Mayo Clinic reports that surgeons often suggest waiting about six months to a year after you stop breastfeeding so the breasts reach a stable size and shape.
- **No smoking, or the ability to stop.** Nicotine reduces blood flow to the skin and raises the risk of wound problems and tissue damage.
- **Support at home.** ASPS strongly recommends help with childcare and household tasks in the early weeks.

A surgeon may suggest waiting, simplifying the plan or splitting it into two stages if you are still losing a lot of weight, plan another pregnancy, have a body mass index of 30 or more, have diabetes or heart disease that is not well controlled, take blood thinners or have a history of clots. None of these is an automatic "no" for everyone, but each one changes the balance of risk.

Previous C-section? Mayo Clinic notes that the old scar can often be incorporated into the new tummy tuck incision.
technique:
### What a mommy makeover can combine

- **Tummy tuck (abdominoplasty).** Removes loose skin and fat, mostly between the navel and the pubic area, and tightens the fascia over separated abdominal muscles (rectus diastasis). Details on the [tummy tuck page](/en/procedures/tummy-tuck/).
- **Breast surgery.** A lift repositions sagging tissue and the nipple; implants restore lost volume; a reduction removes weight; a lift and implants can be combined. See [breast augmentation](/en/procedures/breast-augmentation/) and [breast lift and reduction](/en/procedures/breast-lift-reduction/).
- **Liposuction.** Refines the waist, flanks, hips or thighs around the abdominal repair. See [liposuction](/en/procedures/liposuction/).
- **Occasionally**, ASPS mentions fat transfer, labiaplasty or arm and thigh lifts, depending on the goals.

### One operation or two?

Combining procedures means one anesthetic and one main recovery, but a longer operation. Mayo Clinic points out that complication risk rises when liposuction covers larger areas or is combined with other procedures in the same session. That is why the combination is decided case by case: total operating time, your health profile and the amount of work in each area all count. Ask in consultation why a given combination is proposed and what would change if it were staged.

### Anesthesia, incisions and scars

Combined body surgery of this kind is generally done under general anesthesia in a hospital or surgical center; the anesthesia plan for your case is confirmed during evaluation. The tummy tuck scar runs low, along the swimsuit line; breast lift scars usually circle the areola and may extend downward. Scars are permanent, but they typically soften and fade, and Mayo Clinic notes that a tummy tuck scar can take up to a year to fade as much as it will.
suggested_stay_cartagena:
### How long to plan in Cartagena

There is no single stay length for every mommy makeover. Clearance to fly depends on which procedures are combined, whether drains are used, how quickly you are walking comfortably and how the first follow-up visits go. Two published reference points help frame the calendar:

- ASPS suggests waiting **five to seven days** before flying after body procedures such as liposuction or breast augmentation. That is a minimum for simpler surgery, not a target for a combined operation.
- Avianca lists air travel from **14 days after an abdominoplasty** and asks for a medical certificate issued no more than 10 days before the flight. Because most mommy makeovers include a tummy tuck, this becomes the practical floor for many patients flying that airline; other carriers set their own rules.

The number of days recommended for you is confirmed after your evaluation. For a deeper look at stay length, read [how long to stay after a mommy makeover](/en/blog/how-long-to-stay-after-mommy-makeover/).

### Why U.S. patients look at Cartagena

Colombia keeps the same clock all year (UTC−5, no daylight saving time), so video consultations and follow-up messages fit a normal U.S. workday. Cartagena's Rafael Núñez International Airport receives direct international flights, including routes from the United States. The Caribbean climate is hot and humid year-round, which matters when you will be wearing compression garments: plan air-conditioned lodging and loose, breathable clothes.

### Practical checklist before you book

- Travel with an adult who can stay with you, at least for the first days.
- Choose lodging with an elevator or ground-floor access, air conditioning and a bed you can get in and out of without twisting.
- Keep the return ticket changeable until you are cleared to fly.
- Bring your medical history, medication list and any tests requested in advance.
- Ask who to contact after you are home. ISAPS suggests clarifying emergency care abroad and follow-up in your home country before surgery.
risks_specific:
ASPS lists the possible risks of a mommy makeover as including bleeding, infection, poor healing of incisions, hematoma, seroma (fluid under the skin), loss of nipple sensation, difficulty breastfeeding, implant leak, capsular contracture, breast implant–associated anaplastic large cell lymphoma, unfavorable scarring, recurrent skin laxity, fat necrosis, deep vein thrombosis, heart and lung complications, asymmetry, persistent pain, contour irregularities, fat embolism and anesthesia risks. Each component carries its own profile, so the list grows with the number of procedures.

Travel adds one more consideration. Long flights on their own raise the risk of blood clots in the legs and lungs, and ISAPS notes that surgery compounds that risk. This is the main medical reason not to compress the stay.

What lowers risk in practice: an honest medical history (including supplements), stopping nicotine, following instructions on aspirin and anti-inflammatories, walking early—Mayo Clinic describes patients being helped to walk as early as the first day after a tummy tuck—and wearing garments as directed. Seek care promptly for chest pain, shortness of breath, calf pain or swelling, fever, or spreading redness.

*This page offers general information and does not replace an individual medical evaluation.*

recovery_timeline.text: Swelling, bruising, tightness and fatigue are expected, especially when a tummy tuck is included. You may have drains and will wear a garment and support bra. Short, frequent walks are encouraged. Plan for someone else to handle childcare, lifting and driving.

ASPS describes initial recovery after a mommy makeover as typically lasting **two to three weeks**. Discomfort eases, although you may still walk slightly bent. For a tummy tuck, Mayo Clinic notes that many people return to work in about 2 to 4 weeks, depending on how physical the job is.

Activity returns gradually over about **six to eight weeks** (ASPS). Mayo Clinic advises avoiding lifting, straining and quick bending at the waist for the first six weeks after a tummy tuck, wearing an abdominal binder for about 6 to 8 weeks and waiting at least eight weeks before sports. Lifting young children usually waits for your surgeon's clearance.

Contours keep refining as swelling settles. ASPS notes that final results may take **six to 12 months**, and scars continue to fade during the first year. A week-by-week guide is available in [mommy makeover recovery time](/en/blog/mommy-makeover-recovery-time/).

faqs.q: How long do you need to stay in Colombia after a mommy makeover?
faqs.a: It depends on the procedures combined and how recovery goes. ASPS suggests at least five to seven days before flying after body procedures like liposuction or breast augmentation, and Avianca lists travel from 14 days after a tummy tuck with a recent medical certificate. Your surgeon confirms the date after the follow-up visits.

faqs.q: What does a mommy makeover usually include?
faqs.a: Most plans combine a tummy tuck, breast surgery (lift, implants, reduction or lift with implants) and liposuction of the waist or flanks. The exact mix depends on your anatomy and on what can be done safely in one operation.

faqs.q: How long is mommy makeover recovery?
faqs.a: According to ASPS, initial recovery typically lasts two to three weeks, with a gradual return to normal activities over six to eight weeks. Final results can take six to 12 months as swelling resolves.

faqs.q: How much does a mommy makeover cost in Colombia?
faqs.a: The cost depends on how many procedures are combined, operating time, the facility, anesthesia and the follow-up included, so it is quoted after an evaluation. When comparing quotes, ask exactly what each one includes, from garments to post-operative visits.

faqs.q: Can I have a mommy makeover after a C-section?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Mayo Clinic notes that the existing C-section scar can usually be included in the new tummy tuck incision. Significant scar tissue from previous abdominal surgery is reviewed during the evaluation.

faqs.q: Should I wait until I am done having children?
faqs.a: ASPS lists being finished with childbearing as a candidacy criterion, because a later pregnancy can stretch the abdomen and change the breasts again. Many surgeons also recommend waiting several months after breastfeeding ends.

faqs.q: Is it safe to combine several procedures in one surgery?
faqs.a: It can be, when the combination fits your health and the total operating time. Complication risk increases with the size and number of areas treated, so the surgeon may suggest staging the plan instead.
